The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts Albert Clyde-Burton from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending July 31, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, July 31, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending July 31, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of July 31, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when July 31, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held.
